config.title: useLayoutEffect vs useEffect

intro.title: useLayoutEffect vs useEffect
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that demonstrates the difference between the `useEffect` and `useLayoutEffect` hooks by showing how they affect the timing of DOM updates. You'll learn the core concept of how React's rendering lifecycle works, including when effects run relative to browser painting. The main technologies involved are React's built-in hooks for side effects and JavaScript for handling state and DOM manipulation. By the end, you'll understand when to use each hook to avoid visual flickers and ensure smooth user experiences.
intro.usecase: In real applications, useLayoutEffect is essential when you need to measure DOM elements before the browser paints, such as positioning tooltips, dropdowns, or modals based on dynamic content. For example, in a dashboard with resizable panels, you'd use useLayoutEffect to calculate and set panel dimensions immediately after a resize, preventing visual flicker. Conversely, useEffect is ideal for data fetching, analytics, or subscriptions where timing isn't critical to layout, like updating a chart after fetching new data. Understanding this distinction helps developers build smoother, more responsive UIs in products like form builders, interactive tables, or complex navigation menus.

objectives: Implement useEffect to handle side effects after component rendering
Apply useLayoutEffect to synchronously update the DOM before painting
Construct a component that demonstrates the visual difference between useEffect and useLayoutEffect
Configure a state variable that triggers both effect hooks
Manipulate DOM elements directly within useLayoutEffect to prevent layout flicker
Initialize a timing mechanism to visualize the execution order of both hooks
Integrate both hooks in a single component to compare their behavior
